project: FIEND - Financial Intelligence and Evidence Nexus Decisioning
scope_note: Graph covers the RAG model/pipeline plus the full-stack layer (FastAPI, Streamlit, Postgres, Docker, Prometheus/Loki/Grafana) built 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-14. See tasklist.md.
stack_decision: Pluggable provider architecture (4 providers). Switch via LLM_PROVIDER in .env: gemini (Google, primary, gemini-2.5-flash), anthropic (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), openai (GPT-4o/mini), ollama (local; llama3.2 3B default, qwen3:8b 'accurate' option in web UI). Embeddings: BGE-base-en-v1.5 (local, primary), Gemini models/gemini-embedding-001 (fallback). Provider toggled via LLM_PROVIDER in .env. No cost for local providers — Ollama runs offline, zero quota limits.

nodes.label: SEC EDGAR Filings (10-K / 10-Q)
nodes.detail: 30 filings downloaded (15x10-K + 15x10-Q) across 15 companies: AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL, META, TSLA, JPM, GS, BAC, WMT, COST, JNJ, UNH, XOM. Stored as SEC-native HTML in data/raw/, indexed in data/manifest.json. Total: 125.71 MB. Fetched via EDGAR HTTPS API with User-Agent compliance and 0.2s rate-limiting delay. NOTE: edgar_downloader.py and verify_dataset.py (tasklist Phase 0) are not in the repo or git history; data/raw/ is gitignored.

nodes.label: Document Loader / HTML Parser
nodes.detail: SEC filings are HTML (not PDF). Custom parser strips HTML tags, navigation bars, XBRL inline markup, and boilerplate footers. Phase 2 fix: heading detection now scans text lines (not HTML tags) to skip table-of-contents entries. Uses line positions for section boundaries (not text.find). Extracts item_number and part labels with PART propagation. Produces 300 section-Documents from 30 filings with rich metadata.

nodes.label: HTML Table Extraction
nodes.tool: BeautifulSoup4 HTML table parser (filings are HTML, not PDF — no camelot needed)
nodes.detail: Extracts <table> elements separately from main text flow. Converts to markdown tables with context headers (company, ticker, form, filing date, section, caption). Quality filters remove layout tables, checkbox grids, sparse tables. 2,321 tables extracted across 30 filings (4,678 chunks after table-aware splitting). Integrated into loader via include_tables=True flag. Removes tables from prose stream to avoid duplicate figures.

nodes.label: Fixed-size Chunking
nodes.detail: Dumb baseline. CharacterTextSplitter only splits on newlines so chunks without \n can exceed chunk_size. Produces 8146 chunks from 300 section-documents. Avg 866 chars, max 5633.

nodes.label: Recursive / SEC-aware Chunking
nodes.tool:
LangChain RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with SEC_SEPARATORS (PART/Item headings in both cases, then 

, 
, '. ', ' ', '')
nodes.detail: Improved Phase 1 baseline. SEC-domain separator hierarchy respects filing section boundaries. Produces 9472 chunks. Avg 752 chars, max 1000 (respects chunk_size).

nodes.label: Section-aware Chunking
nodes.tool: Custom section-aware splitter with fragment merging + RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter sub-splitting
nodes.detail: Groups documents by filing (ticker+form+date), merges small fragments (<500 chars) within same filing, then sub-splits large sections. Preserves section label on every chunk. Produces 9424 chunks. Avg 756 chars, max 1000.

nodes.label: Financial Metadata Schema
nodes.detail: Manifest captures: ticker, company_name, cik, form, filing_date, report_date, accession_number, file_path, file_size_bytes. Loader propagates these into Document.metadata and adds: source_file, section, section_index, item_number, part, char_count. Phase 2 chunking adds: chunking_strategy, chunk_index, fiscal_year.

nodes.label: Embedding Model
nodes.detail: Phase 1 baseline used bge-small (Gemini quota too low for full corpus). Phase 3 compared bge-small, all-MiniLM-L6, bge-base; bge-base selected (100% Hit@5, 0.971 MRR@5). bge-large and Gemini embeddings were listed as candidates but never evaluated.

nodes.label: Vector Store
nodes.detail: LangChain FAISS (faiss-cpu), persisted under data/vector_stores/ (gitignored). Phase 1: baseline/. Phase 2: fixed/, recursive/, section/ (BGE-small). Phase 3 candidates: embeddings_bge_small/, embeddings_minilm_l6/, embeddings_bge_base/ (champion). Phase 6: text_only/ (15,098 text chunks), table_aware/, tables_bge_base/ and phase6_table_aware/ (16,626 chunks, 4,678 tables). Production + eval default: phase6_table_aware/ (config.py VECTOR_STORE_DIR, evaluate_generation.py --store). table_aware/ and tables_bge_base/ appear to be earlier copies of the table-aware index. eval/phase9_config.json names the index 'phase6_tables_bge_base', which does not exist. phase6_table_aware/ currently holds 17,188 vectors (eval log 2026-10-08), not the 16,626 recorded in Phase 6/7 — the index has been rebuilt since. Verified 2026-10-08 from the docstore: 17,188 chunks = 11,898 text + 5,290 table.

nodes.label: Dense (Semantic) Retriever
nodes.detail: Pure cosine-similarity vector search. Phase 1 baseline retriever. Phase 2 uses it for all three chunking strategy indexes. Production fetches k=20 candidates (pipeline.build_chain).

nodes.label: Keyword Retriever (BM25)
nodes.detail: Sparse keyword retrieval. Essential for financial queries involving exact tickers, numerical values (e.g. '$391.0B'), fiscal year references, and technical GAAP terminology that semantic search may under-rank.

nodes.label: Hybrid Retriever
nodes.detail: Custom RRF EnsembleRetriever (rrf_k=60) in src/finrag/retrieval/__init__.py combining BM25 + dense. Production weights Dense 0.7 / BM25 0.3 (config.py DENSE_WEIGHT/BM25_WEIGHT), selected in Phase 4 (1.000 MRR@5).

nodes.label: Metadata Filtering
nodes.detail: FilteredRetriever + extract_metadata_filter() auto-extract ticker/form/year/section from the query, over-fetch, then filter on Document.metadata (not native FAISS filters). Commit cf38533 stopped cross-company ticker backfill leakage and bypasses the fiscal_year filter (fiscal_year not populated in metadata).

nodes.label: Reranker
nodes.detail: Cross-encoder rescores top-k candidates against the exact query (more accurate than bi-encoder similarity). Runs fully locally — no API key needed. Evaluated at top-20→5 and top-50→5 depths. Production setting: **top-20→5** — best MRR@5 (0.978), perfect table MRR (1.000), nearly matches top-50 NDCG (0.872 vs 0.886) with half the latency (349ms vs 745ms). FIXED 2026-10-08: since 8427ad9 (2026-09-06) the custom EnsembleRetriever truncated to k=5 and production's FilteredRetriever cut to 5 before reranking, so the reranker only reordered ≤5 docs. build_retrieval_pipeline, evaluate_generation.py and evaluate_reranking.py now pass fetch_k (20) through to the reranker. Regression test: tests/test_finrag.py::TestRerankCandidatePool. config.py rerank_top_k=10 is unused (overridden by final_k).

nodes.label: Grounded-Answer Prompt Template
nodes.detail: Phase 8 hardened: source-of-truth only from evidence, per-claim citations [TICKER, FORM, FILING_DATE, SECTION], mandatory refusal for unsupported questions, prohibits speculation, structured Answer:/Evidence: output format. Refusal string constant: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Evaluation harness in eval/evaluate_generation.py with deterministic citation/grounding/format/refusal checks.

nodes.label: LLM (Generation) — Pluggable Provider

tool.ollama: ChatOllama — llama3.2 (3B, 'Fast', default) / qwen3:8b ('Accurate'), selectable in web/app.py via build_chain(model_name=...)

nodes.detail: Pluggable provider architecture via LLM_PROVIDER in .env. Factory pattern with LLMProvider protocol and registry (src/finrag/generation/__init__.py). Switch providers instantly: LLM_PROVIDER=gemini|anthropic|openai|ollama. Rate limiting: local RPM throttle + tenacity exponential backoff on 429. Ollama runs locally (no API key, zero quota). Files: src/finrag/generation/__init__.py, src/finrag/config.py. Model switch (commit 21c4d19, 2026-10-06): FinRAGPipeline.build_chain(model_name=...) swaps the LLM without reloading the index. Strict-scored eval (2026-10-08, rerank 20→5): llama3.2 81.6% / 5.6s avg; qwen3:8b with thinking off 78.2% / 5.5s (17 over-refusals; prompt was tuned on llama3.2); qwen3:8b with thinking on 64.4% / 12.2s (28 over-refusals); qwen3:4b 40.2% / 31s. qwen3's speed gap was entirely its hidden thinking mode: OllamaProvider now passes reasoning=False unless OLLAMA_REASONING=true. Simulated llama→qwen cascade (escalate when llama's answer fails format/citation-grounding checks or refuses): 87.4% at 7.3s avg. web/app.py MODEL_HELP still claims 86%/92% and 6s/12s. config.py dataclass defaults (ollama/llama3.2) differ from from_env defaults (gemini/gemini-2.5-flash); .env.example sets ollama/llama3.2. Speed fixes 2026-10-08: (1) no RPM throttle for ollama; (2) LLM_MAX_TOKENS 4096→768 — llama3.2 occasionally ran to the 4096 cap (~31s), longest legitimate eval answer ≈460 tokens, and max prompt 2,365 + 768 fits Ollama's 4096 ctx; (3) OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=30m (Ollama default 5m unload costs ~2.3-2.8s reload); (4) OLLAMA_REASONING=false. Post-fix eval: llama3.2 85.1% strict, 1.3s avg / 2.3s p90, 6 over-refusals; qwen3:8b 78.2% strict, 2.9s avg / 3.9s p90, 17 over-refusals. Measured per call on RTX 5070 Laptop 8GB (Ollama 0.35.1, 8 production prompts): llama3.2 ~1,690 prompt tok, ~250 output tok typical, 131 tok/s, ~2.1s, 2.4 GiB VRAM; qwen3:8b no-think ~1,810 prompt tok, ~156 output tok, 65 tok/s, ~3.0s, 5.2 GiB VRAM; retrieval+rerank ~0.25s; pipeline cold load ~70s, ~1.5 GB RAM. Both models do not co-reside in 8 GB: Ollama evicts one, model swap costs 4.4s (llama3.2) / 5.0s (qwen3:8b).

nodes.label: LLM Provider Factory
nodes.detail: Runtime provider selection via LLM_PROVIDER env var. Registry maps provider name to class: gemini→GeminiProvider, anthropic→AnthropicProvider, openai→OpenAIProvider, ollama→OllamaProvider. All implement LLMProvider protocol with invoke() method. Rate-limited wrapper applies RPM throttle + tenacity retry. Files: src/finrag/generation/__init__.py (create_llm_provider, get_provider_class, _PROVIDER_REGISTRY).

nodes.label: Rate-Limit Backoff Wrapper
nodes.tool: RunnableLambda with tenacity retry (exponential backoff + jitter) + local RPM throttle
nodes.detail: Wraps Gemini API calls: local RPM throttle (10 RPM) + tenacity retry with exponential backoff + jitter on 429 errors (max 5 attempts, up to 60s wait). Handles daily quota exhaustion gracefully. Implemented as create_rate_limited_llm() in generation module. 2026-10-08: the RPM throttle (min 60/LLM_RPM s between calls = 6s at RPM 10) is skipped for provider=ollama — it was the dominant term in all local eval latencies (~5.5-5.8s). create_rate_limited_llm(rpm=None) disables it; tenacity retry/backoff still applies. Test: TestLocalProviderNotThrottled.

nodes.label: End-to-End RAG Chain
nodes.tool: LangChain LCEL: retriever | prompt | llm | StrOutputParser
nodes.detail: LCEL chain in FinRAGPipeline.build_chain: phase6_table_aware index → BGE-base dense (k=20) + BM25, RRF 0.7/0.3 → metadata filter → cross-encoder rerank → hardened prompt → LLM. Startup loads FAISS + docstore chunks, BGE, one BM25 and one CrossEncoder once (~19s); per query only retrieval (~0.1-0.4s) + LLM.

nodes.label: Evaluation Benchmark
nodes.status: DONE (Phase 3 + Phase 6 expanded + Phase 8 generation set)
nodes.detail: 45 retrieval Q&A pairs in eval/eval_set.json (35 original + 10 table-dependent). Plus 20 generation Q&A pairs in eval/phase8_generation_set.json covering supported numerical/table-dependent/factual, temporal, cross-document, unanswerable (future/absent/unsupported/ambiguous). Each item has id, category, ticker, form, question, target_sections, ground_truth_keywords, expected_answer, requires_table, expected_refusal. Phase 9: 87-question set in eval/phase9_eval_set.json (17 with expected_refusal=true); frozen config in eval/phase9_config.json. nodes.label: Retrieval Metrics
nodes.detail: Recall@k, Precision@k, MRR, Hit Rate@k, Table Retrieval Rate@k, NDCG@k — measured per chunking strategy (Phase 2), per embedding model (Phase 3), per hybrid weight (Phase 4), with/without metadata filtering (Phase 5), with/without table extraction (Phase 6), with/without reranking (Phase 7). Phase 7 reranking: MRR 0.919→0.978 (top-20→5), NDCG 0.847→0.886 (top-50→5), Table MRR 0.833→1.000, Cross-doc Recall 60%→80%.

nodes.label: Generation Metrics
nodes.tool: Custom evaluation harness (eval/evaluate_generation.py) with deterministic checks: citation format/grounding/format compliance, refusal correctness, keyword coverage, per-category breakdown. RAGAS/DeepEval integration pending.
nodes.detail: Deterministic layer: citation regex validation, grounding against retrieved metadata, Answer:/Evidence: format compliance, exact refusal phrase match, keyword coverage. LLM-as-judge layer (RAGAS/DeepEval) for faithfulness/relevance pending. Phase 9 results: Accuracy 51.7%, Grounded 85.1%, Citation validity 75.9%, Format compliance 66.7%, Refusal accuracy 89.7%. Per-category breakdown: supported_numerical, supported_factual, supported_table_dependent, temporal, cross_document, unanswerable_future, unanswerable_absent_company, unanswerable_unsupported_causal, unanswerable_outside_corpus, unanswerable_specific_metric, ambiguous_contradictory. SCORER BUG fixed 2026-10-08: refusals on supported questions were scored correct when the refusal text contained the expected keywords (inflated qwen3:8b from 64.4% to 92.0%). Latest strict results: llama3.2 81.6%, qwen3:8b (no thinking) 78.2%.

nodes.label: Failure Taxonomy
nodes.detail: 7-category taxonomy with 68 failures analyzed on 87-question eval: Over-refusal 41% (28), Format non-compliance 26% (18), Retrieval failure 18% (12), Citation failure 12% (8), Numerical extraction 9% (6), Cross-doc confusion 7% (5), Reranking failure 6% (4). Real examples documented for each category in eval/results/phase9_summary.md and knowledge-graph/phase9_summary.md. Taxonomy reflects the original 51.7% run only; not refreshed after the 2026-10 fixes. knowledge-graph/phase9_summary.md is gitignored and has drifted from eval/results/phase9_summary.md. There is no phase8 summary in knowledge-graph/ (only eval/results/phase8_summary.md).

nodes.label: Explainability / Evidence Trace
nodes.detail: Surfaces dense cosine similarity, BM25 rank, RRF score, and cross-encoder rerank logits per retrieved passage. Claim-to-source attribution: parses answer into claims, maps each citation [TICKER, FORM, FILING_DATE, SECTION] to exact retrieved chunk and table row. Pipeline method query_explainable() returns ExplainableResult with evidence chunks, claim traces, verification status (VERIFIED/PARTIAL/UNGROUNDED/HALLUCINATED), and retrieval diagnostics. CLI inspect_trace.py for console/JSON output. 2026-10-08: reuses the pipeline's preloaded BGE/BM25/CrossEncoder and its retrieved docs (was reloading all three and retrieving twice per query); chunk ids now md5-based and stable.

nodes.label: (Optional) Domain Embedding Fine-tune
nodes.detail: Fine-tune a sentence-transformer on finance Q&A pairs if Phase 3/9 shows off-the-shelf embeddings clearly underperform. Stretch goal. Not required for v1.

nodes.label: Full-Stack Implementation (FastAPI + Frontend + Deployment)
nodes.detail: FastAPI service (src/finrag/api/main.py), Streamlit UI with model switch + citation trace (web/app.py), Postgres query logging (src/finrag/persistence/), Prometheus metrics (src/finrag/monitoring/metrics.py), Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml, Prometheus/Loki/Promtail/Grafana configs and dashboards (monitoring/). Rebranded FIEND→FIEND 2026-09-14 (README, LICENSE); docker-compose, monitoring dashboards, eval scripts and eval/results summaries still say FIEND. Frontend 2026-10-08: started via `streamlit run web/serve.py` — an st.App wrapper whose lifespan hook loads the pipeline (web/resources.py get_pipeline, st.cache_resource) before the server accepts connections; health 200 after ~25s and the first visitor gets a warm pipeline (UI query 1.7s end-to-end vs 18-23s before). Visual design matches samanyu.dev: .streamlit/config.toml (black #000, amber #f59e0b, Michroma via Google Fonts, slate #cbd5e1 text, 4px radius, st.info as neutral cards) plus a small st.html CSS block (white headings, ghost buttons with amber hover glow, terminal-style input, tag-style status pills, amber-edged evidence chunks). .streamlit/config.toml is now tracked and copied into the Docker image; streamlit>=1.63.0 required. Known UI gaps (pre-existing, not fixed): evidence-card f-string bug (see open issues); the UI runs its own in-process pipeline rather than calling the API; sidebar Company/Filing Type filters, reranker/filtering toggles and confidence threshold are not wired into the query; MODEL_HELP accuracy/latency text is stale; Streamlit's file watcher logs a harmless torchvision traceback while scanning transformers.

decisions_log.decision: Primary LLM switched to Gemini API (gemini-2.0-flash) — Ollama retained as fallback
decisions_log.rationale: Gemini free tier (1,500 RPD, 15 RPM, $0) provides superior financial reasoning, table comprehension, and strict instruction following vs. small local models. Pluggable architecture ensures Ollama remains available for offline use. No credit card required.

decisions_log.decision: Primary embeddings switched to Google text-embedding-004 — HuggingFace BGE retained as fallback
decisions_log.rationale: Gemini text-embedding-004 is state-of-the-art quality at zero cost on the free tier. HuggingFace BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 kept as local fallback and as one of the Phase 3 comparison candidates.

decisions_log.decision: Pluggable provider architecture via LLM_PROVIDER env var
decisions_log.rationale: Single .env flag switches between Gemini (online, highest accuracy) and Ollama (offline, zero cost). Enables fair side-by-side comparison in Phase 9 benchmarks.

decisions_log.decision: Table extraction uses BeautifulSoup4 HTML parser (not camelot/pdfplumber)
decisions_log.rationale: SEC EDGAR filings are downloaded as native HTML, not PDF. camelot and pdfplumber are PDF tools and unnecessary. BeautifulSoup4 already in requirements.txt.

decisions_log.decision: SEC EDGAR as primary data source
decisions_log.rationale: Free, structured, legally public, standardised (XBRL/HTML), no scraping required. 30 filings across 15 companies downloaded.

decisions_log.decision: Switched primary embeddings to local HuggingFace BGE (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) for Phase 1 baseline
decisions_log.rationale: Gemini free tier embedding quota (100 RPM / 1,000 RPD) is insufficient for embedding 39,653 chunks — would take ~7 hours at rate limit. Local BGE-small runs on CPU with no quota limits, completes in minutes. Gemini embeddings retained as Phase 3 comparison candidate.

decisions_log.decision: Fixed LangChain 1.3.18 compatibility — EnsembleRetriever/ContextualCompressionRetriever/CrossEncoderReranker imported from langchain_classic instead of langchain.retrievers
decisions_log.rationale: langchain 1.3.18 removed the langchain.retrievers module entirely. langchain_classic 1.0.8 (installed as a dependency) provides the same classes with identical APIs. BM25Retriever remains in langchain_community. This was the root cause of the finrag package failing to import.

decisions_log.decision: Rewrote loader heading detection to use text-line scanning instead of HTML tag scanning
decisions_log.rationale: Previous approach scanned td/th/div/span elements for SEC section patterns, which matched table-of-contents entries. Text-line approach scans the extracted plain text, skips the TOC region (first cluster of short heading-like lines <25 chars), and uses line positions for section boundaries instead of text.find() which matched first occurrence (often in TOC). Now produces 300 clean section-documents with item_number and part metadata.

decisions_log.decision: Implemented section-aware chunking with fragment merging
decisions_log.rationale: The section strategy groups documents by filing (ticker+form+date), merges small fragments (<500 chars) within the same filing to avoid tiny chunks, then sub-splits large sections with RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter. This ensures every chunk retains its section label and the strategy produces a fair structural comparison against fixed and recursive strategies.

decisions_log.decision: Reorganized project tracking files into knowledge-graph/ directory
decisions_log.rationale: Moved knowledge-graph.json and tasklist.md into knowledge-graph/ directory. Created index.json as AI-readable codebase documentation replacing inline docstring comments in source files. All module/file documentation now lives in index.json for AI reference.

decisions_log.decision: Phase 2 chunking experiment complete — recursive strategy selected as default for Phase 3+
decisions_log.rationale: Ran 10-question comparison across all 3 strategies (fixed/recursive/section). All 3 FAISS indexes built with BGE-small. Key findings: (1) recursive and section strategies produce nearly identical retrieval results; (2) fixed strategy doesn't respect chunk_size (max 5,633 chars) making it unpredictable; (3) cross-company contamination is the primary retrieval quality issue (will be addressed by metadata filtering in Phase 5); (4) section metadata (item_number, part) correctly extracted and propagated. Recursive chosen as default due to reliable chunk_size enforcement and SEC-aware separator hierarchy. Results saved to eval/results/phase2_chunking_comparison.json.

decisions_log.decision: Phase 6 table handling complete — Markdown table extraction with context headers
decisions_log.rationale: Implemented robust HTML table extraction (src/finrag/data/table_extractor.py) with quality filters (min rows/cols, fill ratio, numeric density, section context). Extracts 2,321 tables as Markdown with context headers (company, ticker, form, date, section, caption). Table-aware chunking preserves row boundaries, repeats headers. Benchmark: 10 table-dependent questions added (eval_36–eval_45). Table-aware retrieval: 100% Hit@5 on table-dependent questions, MRR 0.760→0.833, 46% table retrieval rate in top-5. No regression on non-table questions (97.8% Hit@5). Index: 16,626 chunks (4,678 tables). Results in eval/results/phase6_table_comparison.json.

decisions_log.decision: Phase 7 reranking complete — cross-encoder reranking with explicit depth/latency trade-off
decisions_log.rationale: Evaluated ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 cross-encoder on Phase 6 table-aware index at three depths: no-rerank (78ms), top-20→5 (349ms), top-50→5 (745ms). Key findings: (1) Top-20→5 achieves best MRR@5 (0.978) and perfect table MRR (1.000); (2) Top-50→5 achieves best NDCG@5 (0.886) and table recall (61.7%); (3) Cross-document recall jumps 60%→80% with top-20→5; (4) Production setting selected: **top-20→5** — best MRR, perfect table MRR, nearly matches top-50 NDCG with half the latency (349ms vs 745ms). Results in eval/results/phase7_reranking_comparison.json and knowledge-graph/phase7_summary.md.

decisions_log.decision: Phase 8 grounded generation infrastructure complete — hardened prompt, generation test set, evaluation harness
decisions_log.rationale: Built hardened RAG prompt with per-claim citations, mandatory refusal (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE constant), structured Answer:/Evidence: output, no-speculation rule. Created 20-question generation test set (eval/phase8_generation_set.json) covering supported/table-dependent/temporal/cross-document/unanswerable categories. Built evaluation harness (eval/evaluate_generation.py) with deterministic checks: citation format/grounding/format compliance, refusal correctness, keyword coverage. Enhanced rate limiter with tenacity exponential backoff + jitter for quota handling. Full evaluation blocked by Gemini 20 req/day quota (resets midnight UTC). Production pipeline: table-aware corpus → filtered hybrid → rerank top-20→5 → hardened prompt → Gemini. Files: src/finrag/generation/__init__.py, eval/evaluate_generation.py, eval/phase8_generation_set.json.

decisions_log.decision: Phase 9 evaluation complete — full benchmark on frozen pipeline with failure taxonomy
decisions_log.rationale: Ran 87-question benchmark on frozen pipeline (table-aware corpus → BGE-base → FAISS → hybrid 0.7/0.3 → metadata filter → rerank top-20→5 → hardened prompt → Ollama llama3.2). Key results: Retrieval Hit@5 90.8%, MRR@5 0.87, NDCG@5 0.82. Generation (Hardened+Rerank): 51.7% accuracy, 85.1% grounded, 75.9% citation valid, 89.7% refusal accuracy. 4-config comparison: Hardened+Rerank 51.7% > Hardened+NoRerank 54.0% > Original+Rerank 0% = Original+NoRerank 0%. Failure taxonomy: Over-refusal 41%, Format 26%, Retrieval 18%, Citation 12%, Numerical 9%, Cross-doc 7%, Rerank 6%. Phase 9 gate PASSED WITH CONDITIONS — system has known limitations (over-refusal on supported questions, cross-document weakness, format compliance) that should be addressed before production.

decisions_log.decision: Post-implementation audit requires production-stack and evaluation revalidation before deployment
decisions_log.rationale: Audit on 2026-09-01 confirmed: (1) the reusable FinRAGPipeline defaults to the old non-table index and does not expose the evaluated top-20→5 reranker path; (2) the generation evaluator sets expected_refusal to false for every Phase 9 item because all 15 unanswerable items lack that field, and it computes keyword coverage without using it in correctness; (3) citation grounding checks independent metadata sets rather than exact document tuples; (4) the retrieval aggregation function is incomplete; (5) provider dependencies, environment configuration, and claimed Phase 9 summary artifacts have drifted; and (6) pytest collection is broken by an import-time CLI script. The existing benchmark files are retained as historical artifacts, but Phase 8/9 generation claims require rerun after remediation.

decisions_log.decision: Generation scorer: refusal never counts as a correct answer
decisions_log.rationale: evaluate_generation.py counted a refusal on a supported question as correct when its explanation contained ≥50% of the expected keywords. qwen3:8b had 24 such cases (reported 92.0%, real 64.4%). Fixed; regression test TestRefusalNeverCorrectForSupported.

decisions_log.decision: Model balance re-measured; qwen3 thinking disabled by default
decisions_log.rationale: qwen3:8b's latency came from hidden thinking (single call 4.9s → 0.8s with reasoning off). Full eval with thinking off: 78.2% at 5.5s avg / 7.3s p90 vs thinking on 64.4% at 12.2s / 24.7s p90 — faster and more accurate. llama3.2 81.6% at 5.6s. Models agree on 60/87; oracle (best of both) 79/87. Simulated cascade llama→qwen escalating on failed format/citation-grounding checks or refusal: 87.4% at 7.3s avg (27 escalations). OLLAMA_REASONING env toggle added to OllamaProvider.

decisions_log.decision: Architecture analysis: cascade vs single model vs LLM-judge on 8 GB GPU
decisions_log.rationale: Retrieval is model-independent (~0.25s); the LLM only writes the answer from 5 chunks. Cascade (llama3.2 answers; deterministic format/citation-grounding/refusal checks; qwen3:8b re-answers on failure) simulated 87.4% strict with ~31% escalation, but on 8 GB VRAM each escalation adds ~12s of model swapping (swap in 5.0s + answer 3.0s + swap back 4.4s) → ~6.2s avg with ~15s spikes; token use ~2,550/query (+30%). An LLM-judge (qwen3:8b grading every llama3.2 answer) runs both models on every query (~4,000 tokens, +100%, swap every query) and is dominated by qwen3:8b answering alone. Sessions are stateless per query (no context growth); limits are the 4096 ctx window, Ollama keep_alive and single-GPU serialization. Decision: apply speed fixes first; after them llama3.2 = 85.1% strict, 1.3s avg / 2.3s p90, 6 over-refusals, qwen3:8b = 78.2% strict, 2.9s avg / 3.9s p90, 17 over-refusals. Cascade only worthwhile on ≥12 GB VRAM where both models stay resident; on 8 GB prefer a single model and fix qwen3:8b over-refusal via a model-specific prompt tuned on a held-out set.

decisions_log.decision: Speed fixes verified; eval harness now uses production throttle policy

Post-fix eval (rerank 20→5, max_tokens 768, no ollama throttle, thinking off): llama3.2 85.1% strict, 1.3s avg / 2.3s p90 (was 5.6s); qwen3:8b 78.2%, 2.9s avg / 3.9s p90 (was 5.5s). Results: eval/results/phase9_generation_speedfix_{llama3_2,qwen3_8b}.json.

decisions_log.decision: Preload retrieval models once; BM25 from FAISS docstore; full-text chunk identity
decisions_log.rationale: (1) RRF dedup key → (source_file, full page_content); explainability _chunk_id suffix → md5(source_file + full text)[:8] (unique per chunk, stable across processes for Postgres); duplicate _chunk_id in pipeline.py removed. Tests: TestChunkIdentity. Colliding chunks 3,338 → 664 (remaining are byte-identical chunks within one filing). Key cost 3.6µs/query. Eval effect within noise: llama3.2 85.1→82.8%, qwen3:8b 78.2→79.3%, numerical +1 each. (2) FinRAGPipeline keeps one BM25 (k=20) and one CrossEncoder, shared by the chain (build_retrieval_pipeline(bm25=, reranker=)) and query_explainable; dense scores use vector_store.embeddings; query_explainable/query_with_evidence generate from already-retrieved docs via self._generate (no second retrieval+rerank). Per-query query_explainable 18-23s → 1.3-6.4s (remainder is LLM). (3) load_production_pipeline builds BM25 from the FAISS docstore (load_documents_from_index) instead of re-parsing 30 filings: 70s → 18.7s (+~10s imports); ~0.8 GiB RSS after load. load_documents_for_bm25 and duplicate load_hybrid_pipeline/build_index/load_index removed. Caveat: after changing chunking the index must be rebuilt, or BM25 searches stale chunks. Note: tests/test_finrag.py::test_build_production_pipeline re-embeds the corpus and writes into data/vector_stores/phase6_table_aware — do not run it casually.
